question.text: In Example 3 (Fund TM), Class B units held from April 1, 2020 to April 15, 2024 are:

answer.text: Long-term (>12 months, classified as equity-oriented Cat III AIF)

explanation.text: The Logic: In Example 3 (Fund TM), Class B units held from April 1, 2020 to April 15, 2024 cover a period of more than 12 months and are classified as long-term for an equity-oriented Category III AIF, consistent with the holding-period table. The Trap: Class C, not Class B, is short-term in the example because its holding period is less than 12 months. "Exempt" and "unclassified" are not the prescribed treatment. Note: The 12-month cut-off is the dividing line between short-term and long-term for equity-oriented investment fund units in this example.
